utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Now, Mr. Saxon, is there any particular matter or are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm ready to continue. Two small matters simply relating to this witness. Can I simply confirm that the witness -- his ear phones are tied to the Albanian interpretation? Can you understand us, Mr. M-012?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can I confirm that we are in public session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, when we stopped yesterday, you were describing what happened to you and some of your neighbours within the Mirkovci police station. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I didn't hear a translation to what the witness's response was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you ever see a man known as Atulla Qaili in the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How well did you know Atulla Qaili?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition that Mr. Qaili was in when you saw him in the -- let me go one step slower. When you saw Atulla Qaili, where were you and where was Mr. Qaili, in what part of the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Atulla Qaili was together with me in the garage of the Mirkovci police station, and he was in a very grave situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit more specific? Can you describe his -- Mr. Qaili's physical condition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. His physical condition was very bad, so much so that it's hard for me to describe it. I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw him, to what state he was reduced. He was covered with blood all over. There wasn't any place or any part on his body that was not covered with blood. He was unable to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you try to help Mr. Qaili in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried, but there was nothing we could do. We were in such a situation that it was impossible for us to do anything for him. We just put our hat over his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, I would like you to just listen to my question and then respond to the question briefly, and then wait for the next question. I think we'll get through this more quickly if you can do that. All right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You say you tried to help Mr. Qaili. What specifically did you do to try to help this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put his head on my lap and tried to stop the bleeding, because there was a lot of bleeding coming out of his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was Mr. Qaili able to speak to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then what happened to Mr. Qaili there in the garage, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing that happened to all of us happened to Mr. Qaili. He was beaten, mistreated the same way as we were, all of us who were there in the police station garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did Mr. Qaili remain in the garage with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what eventually happened with Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eventually, he was taken away and sent to an unknown destination. We asked for the doctors to come to give him some help, but we asked for the first time, the second time nothing happened; and the third time, they came and fetched him, but we don't know where they took him to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, I would like to show the witness Rule 65 ter number 205. It's a photograph, and it's at tab 4 of the materials that you have with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, if you can please take a look at the photograph that you see on the screen in front of you. Do you recognise the person in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And who is that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the morning of the 12th of August, before the police came to the house, did Atulla Qaili look like this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did he look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked like every normal being. He was in a very good condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this photograph into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P187, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How many days did you spend in the Mirkovci police station, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall. In the Mirkovci police station, I stayed from Sunday to Wednesday -- to Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before you had described how you had lost your pants and your underwear at some point near the Brace house, were you able to obtain some clothing at some point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I kept constantly asking to have some clothes, but nobody gave me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What help, if any, did you receive from your neighbours who were held with you in the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them gave me his underwear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So you say you remained in the Mirkovci police station until Tuesday. If you can recall, where did you go on Tuesday, which would have been 14th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of August, they sent us to the court, Skopje Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move into private session very briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you were transported to the court in Skopje, do you know what this court was called? Do you know the name of the court where you were taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only knew it to be "the court," a court, just any court. I didn't know more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you and some of your neighbours arrived at the court, what happened at that moment when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were beaten there, too, by the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were the police wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were in uniform; some were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you say you were beaten. What were you beaten with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With whatever they had, with rubber batons. We were kicked at, anything they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And as you were being beaten, what, if anything, did these policemen say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us that, "You are to blame, that's why you are here. You are the culprits."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you taken inside the court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Without stating their names, did you see anyone who you knew there inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then they started to try us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where were you taken, Witness M-012?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the trial chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you were taken inside, who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the Bench, the prosecutor, and a lawyer that they assigned to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "the Bench," are you referring to a judge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you entered that courtroom and you saw these people, what condition were you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a very, very bad state. I could hardly stand on my feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And was there any discussion amongst these people when you went into that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What were they talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were talking about me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you be a little bit more specific, please? What were they discussing about you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I recount it in detail? They were discussing about me why I was without any clothes, why I had the injuries on me, and if they did release me, what do the papers say about that? One of them said, "Send him to -- remand him in custody for 30 days. Maybe he will get better, and then we will see what to do with him."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why, if you heard, why were these people concerned about what would happen if you were released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was in a very precarious health condition. My body was filled with injuries. It had become blue all over. My eye -- one of my eyes was almost closed. I had problems with my kidney. My feet were aching. As I said, I was in a very, very bad state.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What I need your help with, if you can help us, please, you said these people said something about "if they release me, what do the papers say about that." What papers are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to local newspapers or international newspapers. They might write about the treatment given to us, because we needed medical assistance and not to be taken to the court or to be sent to jail. We should be in hospital, given the condition we were in, because we were in a very, very serious condition. It's hard for me to describe to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And what did these -- what, if anything, did these gentlemen tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us that we would be taken into custody, pre-detention unit, and then they asked me how come I have such bruises and injuries all over my body.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you were in this courtroom with these people, what accusations, if any, did they make against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear any accusations. I only know that we were sent to 30 days of imprisonment in Shutka Prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, at any point on the 12th of August, did you have -- were you in possession of a weapon, a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you in possession of any ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show the witness what is tab 5 in your binder, and if this exhibit could not be published to the public, because we are in public session and it might identify the witness. This is 65 ter number 10.25. It has ERN number 0463-8824.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to please take a look at the Macedonian version of the document that's on the right side of your computer screen.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, I would like to ask you to please take a look at the right side of the computer screen in front of you. It shows the Macedonian version of this document. Are you able to read some in the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document says, at the top, "Ministry of Interior, OVR Cair." It's dated 12th of August, 2001, Skopje. It's called "Certificate on Temporary Seized Possessions," and it reads: "On the day of 12 August 2001, at the police station Mirkovci," and then we see a name there. I won't say it at this time because we're in public session. Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Born on a particular birth-date. Is that your birth-date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it says: "The authorised person," and then there's a blank, "seized the following possessions in temporary custody." And then on line 1, it says: "41 bullets for a Thompson-calibre 45," "Thompson automatic rifle" in the English version. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have any such bullets in your possession on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can ask the audio-visual group, please, to actually let us see a bit more of the bottom of the Macedonian version. We need to see the bottom of it. Thank you, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, we see a signature. In the middle, we see a stamp. On the left-hand side, it says: "Possessions were seized by," and then there's a name written there. Can you just tell us, is that your name that's written there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my name, but this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So you did not sign this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Already you'll find that tab 5 is now Exhibit P46, Mr. Saxon. The big motion to admit documents from the bar table included this one, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Your Honour. Until this moment, I was not aware that there was a decision, but, obviously, there was and I need to read it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it could give you some bedtime reading tonight, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will keep you awake for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. My wife is away, so I have a good excuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, I'd like to go back to the time when --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My apologies again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to the time on the 14th of August when you were in the court in Skopje. All right? Can you turn your mind to that for a minute?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness what is tab 6, which is 65 ter number 10.37, ERN number 0463-8846 to 8847. Before I go on, can I just confirm that the last exhibit is admitted under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And so is this one, and this is part of P46 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Very well. Can this not be published to the public, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, you see the document on the right side of your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a document. At the top, we see the date "14 August 2001." We see the words -- we see a name there. Can you confirm that that's your correct name under the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see the words "Velce Pancevski, Dobre Efremovski, Rumena Kostadinova."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the second page, please? The document that is on the screen does not appear to be the document that we need. We need the second page of this prior -- this statement. It should have ERN 0463-8847. I think it's coming now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just have a few questions for you, Witness M-012, about the contents of what's written here. It says: "Started at 1540 hours," and then in the second paragraph, it says: "Pursuant to Article 210, paragraph 2, the accused was informed that the basic public prosecution had delivered a request on the enforcement of investigation with the proposal to impose detention." Do you see that? Do you see where I'm reading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in the next sentence, it says: "Thus, because of the well-based suspicion, he committed a criminal act of terrorism pursuant to Article 313." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just for the record, have you ever been a member of a terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I've never been a member of any group or political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Have you ever committed any acts of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But at this time, you were accused of such conduct; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do accuse me. They can write whatever they want on this paper, but this does not refer to me because I am a loyal citizen of that state. I am clean. I have done nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please go two paragraphs further down. There's a big paragraph in the middle of the page, and it says, in sort of the second sentence, it says: "The accused stated before this court, before the investigative judge"?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Whoever is working, it would be the next paragraph down, please, the large paragraph beginning: "Pursuant to Article 3." That's correct. And on the Macedonian version, if you go down a bit, up a bit. Right there. Go down a bit. And if you start enlarging there, then the witness will be able to see it. Scroll down. That's it right there. That's enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says, Witness, in that paragraph: "I am beaten up by the police." I should say before that, it also says: "The accused stated before this court, before the investigative judge, 'I am beaten up by the police because of the incident that happened on Sunday, 12 August 2001 .'" And it says: "I have injuries on my face. My right eye is closed with a bloody hematoma and bruise. My right eye is damaged and my vision ability is bad. My nose is injured, and, especially, I have bodily pains in the region of my kidneys. I was beaten all over my body, and today I am brought in the court before the investigative judge in my T-shirt and underwear only," et cetera, et cetera. Can you tell us, please, Mr. M-012, is this a roughly accurate description of the injuries that you had at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you look down at the very bottom of the page, you see the word "accused" at the bottom. Do you see that word in the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then there appears to be a signature there underneath that word "accused." Do you see that signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that document can be removed now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, after the court, where, if anywhere, were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the court, I was taken to the Shutka Prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Who took you to the Shutka Prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And were you taken there all by yourself or were there other detained persons with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Others as well, other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into private session for a moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you arrived, you and this group arrived at Shutka Prison, what happened when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived there, they ordered us to make a statement, a written statement, saying that allegedly we were beaten by the fellow villagers, but I did not want to do that. I wanted to say the truth, that we were beaten by the police; and what happened in the prison was the same as what happened previously, we were beaten by the police in prison as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's go a little bit more slowly, please. When you say, "They ordered us to make a statement," saying that you and your neighbours had been beaten by fellow villagers, who ordered you to make such a statement? Do you know the identity of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him very well. Do you want me to mention his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was referred as Commander Zivko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: While you were in the prison, what medical treatment, if any, did you receive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I allowed to respond? I didn't receive any medical treatment except for a pill called Analgin, and they cleaned my eyes with a sort of a liquid spray. Apart from these two things, I didn't receive any other medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how much time did you spend, approximately, in that prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, while you were in Shutka Prison, did anyone from the police or Ministry of Interior come and ask you questions about what had happened to you on the 12th of August or after the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Anyone from the public prosecutor's office or from any investigative judge? Did anyone come and ask you about these events while you were in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After you were released from prison after four months, did anyone from the police, Ministry of Interior, public prosecutor's office, any investigative judge, attempt to contact you to speak to you about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, not at all. Up to this date, nobody came to ask me about the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "nobody," you're referring to no one from the Government of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Nobody from the Government of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I need to step back for a moment and go back to that Sunday morning, the 12th of August, and just clarify a point. You had explained that you and some other men were in the basement of your house, and then the police arrived. Were there any women in that basement at the time the police arrived, where you were? Were there any women in the basement where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were not any women in the basement where I was, but they were in the basement in the house nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just to help us understand, why were men and women staying in different basements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that basement was safer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Which basement was safer, the basement where the men were or the basement where the women were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basement where the women were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At any point, did some of the men visit the women in the basement for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, continuously, because they were scared. We would go and see how they were doing. We would play a little bit with the children just to make them not frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, after what happened to you in August of 2001, do you still feel any effects from that treatment, from that experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question? I do not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's my fault. It means I didn't ask a clear question. I'll try to rephrase it. You've mentioned some injuries -- you mentioned injuries that you received on the 12th of August, 2001, and on the days after that. Since that time, can you describe how your health is today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My health condition is disastrous. I have permanent headaches, my body aches, and these wounds will never go away. I do not hope -- I do not think that these consequences will ever heal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How do you sleep at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot sleep at all. You might not believe me, but I can't. I have problems with my sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before the 12th of August, did you suffer from these problems that you've just described? The 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never had any health problems. My body was clear as a crystal. I never visited any doctor, because there was no need to. I was perfectly healthy, physically and psychically.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Before the 12th of August, were you able to work on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes, regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Since August of 2001, are you able to work regularly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, M-012. I am Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Guenal Mettraux, I'm defending Mr. Boskoski. Because of some of the questions I have, I ask to move into a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The documents are not being displayed to the public at the moment, only photographs. So as long as you're careful in your questioning, we should be able to continue in public session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the text of your statement has been translated, is it true that you signed not only the first but also the other pages of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Maybe I did sign, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that the witness is shown the second page of this text. It might be 1D0513. Your Honours, I apologise. It is possible that -- that we should now go on to document 65 ter number 1D39, page 1D0467, and the Macedonian version -- no, no, no. 1467. Can we see the other page, 1D067?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told there is some temporary technical problem which is attempting to be resolved, which is preventing the publication of the document you want onto the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. I would not look for the number now, not to hold up the witness. The witness said he does not remember. By showing the page, probably we would remind him. But I would now like to ask that document 65 ter number 1D39, page 1D074 is shown, the Macedonian version 1D0485.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, do you recognise your signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that when giving this statement and the later statements to the investigator of the Prosecutor, after being read the statement, you have signed that you give the statement on your free will and that everything you have said is the truth according to your best recollections; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The second statement given to the investigator of the Prosecutor was given by you on 4th of November, 2004; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I will ask that the witness is shown document 65 ter number 1D40, page 1D0487.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If it would help my colleague and help speed up the process, the Prosecution is willing to stipulate to the dates of these statements, if that would help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Defence may be assisted by that, Mr. Saxon. Ms. Residovic, the Prosecutor says that he can agree to the dates of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that then we don't need to show the aforementioned document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. M-012, that in April of this year, in Ljuboten, you saw the documents that were shown to you by the investigator of the Prosecutor of the ICTY and that your comments regarding those documents were noted down, and that after that you have signed also those comments regarding the documents you were shown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you were shown the documents, you then made additional comments and corrections to your previous statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I did. There were probably some typing errors or some translation mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now move to the questions asked to you yesterday by my colleague with regards to the events. When you were answering the questions of my learned colleague about the people -- who were the people who requested from you to go out of the basement of the house of (redacted), you stated that it was the police. And the question to describe the uniform, if you remember, you stated that those were camouflage uniforms, black uniforms, and all sorts of uniforms that the police is wearing, as recorded on page 70 of the unofficial transcript. Do you remember that you have said this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A redaction, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for the caution. I will try not to mention a name later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, Mr. M-012, is it correct that you have recognised the uniforms those persons were wearing only based on the colours that you have described answering the question of the learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-012, at that time, the Army of the Republic Macedonia was wearing both camouflage and black uniforms; were you familiar with this fact as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the army. I don't know that the army was wearing black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. M-012, is it correct if I were to say that actually, in 2001, you did not know the structure of the army and neither of the police of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. I do know them because I live there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. M-012, you mean to say that you were familiar with the complete organisation that the police had and the Army of the Republic of Macedonia as well in 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please? I'm not clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, since you stated that you knew that because you were living there, my question is: Have I understood you well? You then, in 2001, knew the complete structure and the organisation of the police and the Army of the Republic of Macedonia. Was that what you have just confirmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you then did not know the organisation and the structure of neither the army nor the police at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it. What you want me to say, in what respect, do I know them?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe a bit more precise. Did you know what were the special competencies belonging to the individual bodies of the police or the individual body of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to say that you didn't know also what were the exact bodies in the Republic of Macedonia that had the duty to run the investigation, you could agree with this again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can that question be clarified? The translation was "the duty to run the investigation." Can it be clarified what investigation my colleague is speaking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that needs clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, were you, as a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia, familiar with the notion that it is only the courts that are running investigations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not informed of that, but, normally, I think it's a court that should do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So my question is: Is it correct, considering your answer as well, that you do not know precisely all competencies of the bodies that are in charge of the investigation in the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is the court's responsibility to conduct investigations. As far as I know, it should be done through the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you don't have any knowledge about the body superior to the courts in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You surely, considering your profession and the life you led in Ljuboten, were not able to know at that time what were the tasks and the competencies of the prosecutors of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The answer is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also do not know who would be the body superior over the work of the prosecutors in the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, because I know that it's the Ministry of Justice that leads the work of the prosecutor's office. I think it's up to the Ministry to do this, because there is a Ministry of Justice in every state that must guide the work of the prosecutor's office. This I know very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you, Mr. M-012, to go back to a previous question, because the interpreters are reminding us that in -- that one of my previous questions was not recorded -- the answer was not recorded in the transcript. So I will ask you to answer me again. Namely, I have asked you that considering your profession and the life you led in Ljuboten, is it correct that in 2001, you did not know what were the tasks and the competencies of the prosecutor in the Republic of Macedonia? So please answer this, because your answer was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks and the powers of the prosecutor's office should be known by the Ministry of Justice because they are under its jurisdiction. It's one of its bodies, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague has asked you about your arrival to the court in Skopje, and you then mentioned that there was some police there. Tell me, is it correct that you do not know to which body is the police that operates within the court building attached?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police is under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Interior. It's one of its bodies; whereas, the court falls into the Ministry of Justice jurisdiction. This I know very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later, you stated that you have been in a prison, and it is there where you encountered police or prison guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prison guard. I described -- by the word "police," I refer also to the prison guard, because they were wearing uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also do not know what is the body superior to the prison guards and the prison itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. I know who is the superior body. I know that the Ministry of Interior also has responsibility over the prison, as well as the court. I know this very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the laws of the Republic of Macedonia would stipulate differently from your testimony, you would still remain with your answer that you have just given previously?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Can you be more explicit, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm withdrawing the question and I will not ask you this question, because your knowledge about the legislation are probably not of the sort that you would be able to fully answer my question. Now, Mr. M-012, we would move to some other questions that you have discussed yesterday and also previously with the investigators of the Prosecution. As a citizen of the Republic of Macedonia, you were aware that in 2001, there was a conflict between certain Albanian groups, especially in the regions of Kumanovo and Tetovo, and that those events were broadcasted also via the Macedonian television; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're also familiar that because of the deterioration of the security situation and the crisis in the country, the Army of the Republic of Macedonia has deployed its forces around Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that the Army of Macedonia, because of the special strategic importance, that the area of Ljuboten and Skopska Crna Gora, on the slopes of which Ljuboten is located, are of the special importance for the security of the city of Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe this would be the right time to take recess, because I will then start asking questions directly related to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We must have our first break at this time because of the tapes, and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon. Oh, I beg your pardon. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, before we move on to events in Ljuboten, with regards to the previous questions, just an additional clarification. When my learned colleague asked you questions about your interrogation in the court, you were shown the minutes from that interrogation. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Can you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My colleague, the Prosecutor, when examining you, showed you minutes -- a record from the investigating judge in the court in Skopje. Do you remember that my colleague showed you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You then stated that there were the judge, the prosecutor, and, if I understood you well, an attorney there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have answered my question, that you knew that above the prosecutor's office the superior body was the Ministry of Justice and that this is a generally-known fact; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You must know, then, that in 2001 the Minister of Justice in Macedonia was Mr. Hixhet Mehmeti; did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you now what you probably know, that on the 10th of August, 2001, not far from Ljuboten, at the Ljubotenski Bacila locality, a landmine caused the deaths of several members of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia and several others were injured. Are you familiar with that? ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard about this event from the media and television, but this location is not nearby. It's about ten kilometres far from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The news about the landmine that was placed and the consequences clearly indicated that the mine was placed by the Albanian terrorists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who laid those mines, but the two parties should know who did that. I was a simple civilian. I was looking after my family and was not interested in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe my question, Mr. M-012, was not clear enough. I'm not saying that you know, but is it correct that the media, the TV and the other media, informed the public that those mines were placed there by the Albanian terrorists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-012, that on that date armed people, who participated in the placing of the mine, entered the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-012, that on that date, on the Friday, the 10th of August, 2001, people who participated in the placing of the mine entered the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a lie. There were no people of that kind in Ljuboten. Only this massacre was committed in Ljuboten. Only the civilians or residents of Ljuboten, men, women, elderly, children, were in Ljuboten. No other people were in Ljuboten. Whatever information that you are putting to me is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-012, that the situation brought about disturbance among the citizens, and one part of the inhabitants left Ljuboten on the Friday and the Saturday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Part of the inhabitants of the village of Ljuboten left Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who could leave left, and they left because of the shooting coming from different types of weapons used by the Macedonian army and police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that your wife, with your young son, also left Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. That should be redacted, and I now move that we go into a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-012, that on the Saturday there was an agreement in the village to organise check-points and resistance if someone would enter the village to make searches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you. Please repeat your question and clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. M-012, that on the Saturday a meeting was held with the village leaders; whereby, it has been agreed that check-points are organised and to give resistance to those that would enter the village in order to search it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-012, that in that moment, Commander Lisi said that he is the one who will take the responsibility about the situation in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I don't know who Commander Lisi is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that on that day, all adult men were distributed a certain quantity of bullets in case that someone would enter the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. If we had weapons or if we had an organisation in the village, I wouldn't have been captured by them. This is a misinformation. It has nothing to do with the reality. There was nobody armed in Ljuboten. Only a massacre was committed there. The whole world should know that only a massacre and a genocide was committed in Ljuboten against people, elderly, women, children. A six-year-old child was killed, and he was completely innocent. We were all civilians, innocent residents in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, you just mentioned that a six-year-old boy was killed. Could you confirm that that kid died on the Friday, 10th of August, from a shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know the person by the name of Baki Halimi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as to everyone else in the village, you also knew that Baki Halimi was called Commander Lisi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. Baki Halimi is a history teacher. He was not a commander. He is only a teacher. This is misinformation that you're putting to me. Maybe to you these are arguments, but for me they are not. They are completely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. M-012, is it correct that it is in line with Albanian tradition that men possess weapons that was earlier mainly used for certain festivities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that the witness is shown document 1D40, 1D0490. I will -- let me just see. We have the Macedonian text here. No, there is no Albanian; there is only Macedonian text here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that exactly in this statement of yours, you mentioned that it is correct that there's a cultural tradition of the Albanians to possess weapons in the house and to only use it during festivities; is that what you have earlier said? This is your statement of 4th of November, 2004.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this does not apply to the 21st century. This applies to the past, when the Albanians had the tradition to do this during festivities and celebrations. In the 21st century, there's no room for weapons. There's only room for pencils and learned people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can also confirm, Mr. M-012, that after these events, also events of August in 2001, in the village of Ljuboten and in the surroundings of the village, an additional hidden weapon was found, although there was no conflict in the area anymore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you: Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this very page of the statement of the 4th of November, 2004, you were asked about whether there was a meeting of the leaders. You said there was no time for such a meeting to be held, but people were only meeting individually, discussing whether -- is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke only with those who were in the same basement with me. I had no opportunity to speak with any other person, and I already told you that. You should know it for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, if you have stated something else earlier, then your statement differs from the statements -- from the statement that you are giving now before the Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. If we can simply be directed a little bit more precisely to which part of this statement my colleague is referring to, perhaps a paragraph number or a page. I see it now. I believe my colleague is referring to paragraph 17. Yes, it looks like 17 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I interpreted the question in order to gain some time, thinking that the question [as interpreted] can answer that question. Thank you for the assistance of my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My last question would be -- was: Is it correct that your statement about the mentioned facts given today before the Tribunal and the statement that you have previously given to the investigator of the Prosecution are differing about these facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it would be more helpful if my learned colleague could be a bit more precise, point out particular facts. I'm not sure if this witness can answer that question the way it was phrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He may be able to answer generally; but if not, it will be necessary to look particularly, if Ms. Residovic wishes to pursue it. So proceed with your question, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, is it correct that your statement given today before the Court, regarding the traditional possession of arms and about the individual meetings with the people after the mine incident, is different than the statement given to the investigators of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Unless I'm confused by the translation, I believe there may be a problem with this question, because I don't believe I asked any questions of the witness about the ethnic Albanian culture, nor about meetings with people after the mine incident. So this strikes me as a very confusing question to be asked to this witness this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's a fair observation, Ms. Residovic, because you're referring in this question, it seems, to the traditional possession of arms; and the first the Chamber has heard of it is your questioning just now, so there seems to be no previous evidence before us from this witness about that matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. I asked the witness today about that fact and I later pointed out to him what he has said to the investigators of the Prosecution in his statement, and I did not mention that the learned colleague asked the witness about it before this court. So I'm asking about the difference between what he said before and the answers he gave to my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I find it confusing. I don't know how the witness will manage. I suspect if you want to pursue this, you might have to put to him some specific aspects.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is some confusion, I would just address the witness again with the question, whether is it correct that in his previous statement, he stated, in point 20 of the documents shown to him, that it is true that the cultural thing or tradition is to possess arms in a house, but it is only possessed in order to be used during festivities. On my question, the witness previously answered that it is not the tradition of the Albanians, and, therefore, my additional question came whether his answer of today and the answer that he had given before are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood differently the answer of the witness. I understood him to say it is not in the 21st century the tradition of the Albanians, but it was the tradition earlier. If that helps, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let me go on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, at the questions of my learned colleague, you explained that after being taken out of the basement, that you were ordered to lie on the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were all lying in a small place -- a small space; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And although you were facing the ground, you were able to hear everything that the others were saying and all the words that were directed to the others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you had T-shirts over your head, you were not able to see everything precisely; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the moment while you were lying, no one put a knife under your throat and said that they are going to slaughter you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They put the knives on our throats, this is correct, and the barrels of their weapons into our mouths. You should believe everything I'm saying to you, because everything I'm saying is accurate. The knives on our throats, the barrels of the guns into our mouths, and many other things that happened there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that moment, Mr. M-012, no one entered other premises, especially nobody entered the mosque; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't have a chance to go to the mosque. Whoever was there, ask him or her to come and testify.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At this moment, I'd like to ask you to answer to the questions that you have answers to. Please tell me, Mr. M-012, is it correct that about putting the knife under your throat, you never testified in your previous statements about it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can never tell everything at one time. You don't have the time. You don't remember things. Now that I am here, even now I cannot tell everything. Everything you ask about something, you will certainly say something more or something less, because you cannot describe the entire reality. It will take such a long time, and I'm sure one will be always unable to describe everything one has gone through.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering to the questions of my colleague, the Prosecutor, regarding the death of Sulejman Bajrami, yesterday, you said that first money was taken away from her [as interpreted] mother and other possessions - that's pages 74, line 18 and 19 on the official transcript - and then you were ordered to walk - page 75 from the unofficial transcript - and that then Sulejman Bajrami was killed. Is that what you yesterday said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is completely accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you have given on the 4th of November, 2004, you have described that event in the following manner: "Some of the police officers have shouted from the yard, 'Who is Sulejman? He's free to go. He can join his mother.' Sulejman got up and started walking. I think it was a mistake that he went towards the street and not towards the yard." Is it correct that you have said this in the statement that you have given to the investigator of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not wrong that he walked along the road and didn't come back. Maybe the interpreter didn't take down every single word I said. Whatever I said in the statement is accurate from what concerns his mother to him, and there are live arguments to prove what I am saying. Everything is accurate. Even if I were to write everything in the order of events, the paper wouldn't suffice to write everything. There are many ways of describing or writing down an event.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that these two statements are not identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are identical. For me, they are identical. Maybe not for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct, you could agree with me that actually, Sulejman Bajrami was trying to escape, and only after that he was shot at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't try to escape. This is not true. Sulejman Bajrami didn't go anywhere. They killed him without any reason at all. He didn't have the strength to leave. It was impossible. It was impossible for him to leave. He didn't stand a chance. He was deliberately killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. M-012, could you tell me, what position was his father in, Aziz Bajrami?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was near him, near all of us, actually, outside the gate of the yard. We were all lying down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were all lying down. So when you said yesterday that you were ordered to walk and that you started walking, which is written on page 85, that statement of yours would not be correct at that time because you were all still lying down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you allow me to describe everything in detail, whatever happened? Is it possible for me to describe the van, exactly what happened?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me now, how was Aziz Bajrami wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Aziz Bajrami said, "Oh, my son, they killed you," and he was shot at and wounded simply because of these few words. He said to his son, "Oh, son, say something to me. They killed you." That was the only thing he did that he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that Aziz Bajrami, in his statement of the 6th of November, 2004, said to the investigator of the Prosecution that: "At the moment when I was hit in my hand, I was kneeling. My head was on the ground, and my both hands were in front of my head when the bullet caught me," and that his son was hit after that, would that statement be a different one to the one that you are now giving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is true, but he will come here. He will explain to you in greater detail. This is what I know. This is what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now, Mr. M-012 - and we may move into a public session - ask you several questions that are not directly related to the event. Tell me, is it correct that the brothers, Rafiz and Shefajet Bajrami, were members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just wondering, would it be helpful to identify a time frame that my learned colleague is speaking about, or is she asking ever?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2001, before the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer this question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat it, please. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That the brothers Bajrami, Rafiz and Shefajet, were members of the NLA before August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were the brothers, Rafiz and Shefajet Bajrami, members of the NLA after August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were the brothers Bajrami, Rafiz and Shefajet, inside the village on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation] .

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I was to tell you that Shefajet was a member of the special unit of Commander Teli -- excuse me, your answer to the previous question was not recorded. I have asked you whether the brothers Bajrami [as interpreted] and Rafiz were after the events, whether they were in the village that day. Your answer was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Rafiz was in Italy, Shefajet was in Kosovo, working there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to suggest to you, Mr. M-012, that Shefajet Bajrami, nicknamed "Shef" belonged to the special unit of Commander Teli, who was murdered [as interpreted] at the beginning of August in Skopje, you could recall that he was actually a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe this. I didn't see this with my own eyes. He didn't say anything to me. Nobody said anything, and I didn't have the right to ask what he was doing. I think it's everyone's right to do whatever he or she wants. It's not my duty to ask about such things, what they are doing, what are they engaged in. But I do know for sure that Shefajet was working in Kosovo and Rafiz was in Italy, working too. This is all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, with your leave, page 44, line 10, my question about the demise of the Commander Teli was translated as "murdered." Well, I think it would be correct to say "killed." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you have answered again that to your knowledge, Shefajet at that time was in Italy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rafiz was in Italy; Shefajet was in Kosovo. He went there to work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If in some of the statements one of his brothers would claim the opposite from you, he would then not be telling the truth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you think? What do you mean? I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe we are in public session; and if that's the case, I believe the name of someone needs to be redacted on page 50 from perhaps lines 8 to 13 and, again, perhaps 14 to 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, and I apologise. We do not have on our screen the logo telling us whether we are in a public or a closed session at all times, so I thank my colleague for this caution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. M-012, is it correct that after the killing of Teli, his commander, Arusha, in revenge for this killing, placed the mine at Ljubotenski Bacila, together with his associates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an ordinary citizen. You should know I was not a member of any organisation or political party. There was no way I could know plans either of NLA or the Macedonian army. I was just a random victim, so please don't ask me such provocative questions. How can I know secrets of an army? I was, as I said, a rank-and-file citizen, so I don't know anything about what you are putting to me. I was simply worried about my family affairs. Had I been interested in national questions, I would have been there, not staying in my own house and being treated and subjected to such inhumane treatment. So I kindly ask you to know this, that I am a rank-and-file loyal citizen worried only about his family and thinking about how to feed his family.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in relation to this, one more last question: Were you aware then, on the 10th, 11th and 12th of August, 2001, that Shefajet, with a group of the Commander Arusha, participated in the placing of the mine, and that together with two armed people arrived to the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I don't know that he was in the army, let alone to know that he has put a mine or not. I was not in a position to be told such things, to be told secrets, or what else. I was a simple -- an ordinary citizen. This is not right. This is not accurate. I don't know Commander, as you are saying, Arusha, or Teli, or I don't know Commander Rabbit. I don't know these persons. I've come here to tell you what I know personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you could answer my questions briefly, saying "yes" or "no," and it is not necessary for you to make elaborate explanations if that is not really necessary. I would like to ask you now, Mr. M-012, to confirm that it is correct that while you were inside the police station Mirkovci that because of the fact that some of the detainees did not feel well, the police has twice -- has invited doctors to examine you twice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called, but they were not doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the situation of Atulla Qaili deteriorated, then the police called an ambulance again and he was transferred to hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was transferred. When police came, Atulla Qaili was almost dead. In my opinion, I could take him for a dead person.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague showed you the photograph that you recognised as the photograph of the late Atulla Qaili. You personally did not know who has taken this photograph and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in jail at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But in the photograph you were shown, you were able to see a cut, a slash across the neck that would indicate that a postmortem was performed on the body. Have you seen that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you know that several days later, because his name was incorrectly written, he was transferred from the mortuary and buried in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name -- last name was deliberately changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The photograph that you were shown also displays the postmortem lividity that is developed in any body of a dead person after a certain time; are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph, yes. As you say, if you say that that's correct, then we'll leave it that way, but personally I don't know where and by whom was this photograph taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have, answering my question, stated that, yes, the police called an ambulance, but that those who arrived were not doctors. You never verified the identity or the expertise of those persons who came there in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't do anything. They just took his pulse, and among themselves they said, "It's over with him. He's dying." I don't know where they took him. Had they been real doctors with a real ambulance car, they would have had the appropriate equipment with them. I didn't see any sign that would indicate that they were doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I have asked you not about the fact when Atulla Qaili was taken to hospital, but before that, when doctors arrived, called by the police, those who examined you. You then stated that you did not believe that those were doctors. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not doctors, in my opinion; but they called them doctors. They referred to them as doctors.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you whether Atulla Qaili was transferred from the mortuary somewhat later and buried only then because of the mistake in the name, you stated that the change in the name was deliberate. Tell me, was it through some investigation that you are certain that someone changed the name of Atulla Qaili deliberately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at the police station; and pursuant to the methods and procedures followed by the police, it would have been very easy for the police to verify his identity, his full name and last name. The police was in position to identify him, to know his exact name and last name, but they didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, when you went out of detention, you never filed criminal charges against the persons who ill-treated you or against the persons you indicated in your statements to the investigator or before this court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you have never asked your counsel to file criminal charges against a person; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never filed a report with the police, with the Prosecutor, or any other body, noting the names of the persons who took you out of the basement, ill-treated you, brought you to the police station Mirkovci, and ill-treated you there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not file any charges against anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally considered that it was completely sufficient for you to give a statement to the OSCE, the International Committee of the Red Cross, or the investigators of this Tribunal, and that they will then file such charges or reports on your behalf; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only told my story to these organisations that you mentioned in the latter part of your question, because I trusted them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the last question: Since you did not trust Macedonian police, after the events, you never wanted to discuss things with the Macedonian police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
