utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. M-012. Your Honours, I have finished the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this witness will be cross-examined by my colleague, co-counsel, Jasmina Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed, thank you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering that this is the first time I'm addressing the Court, I wish to introduce myself. My name is Jasmina Zivkovic, and together with my learned colleague, Antonio Apostolski, I am the defence counsel for Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today I will ask questions of Witness M-012 regarding the events in the village in Ljuboten on the 10th to 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness M-012, you heard my name. I am defence counsel for Johan Tarculovksi. I will now ask you some questions that my learned colleague, Edina Residovic, did not ask. Are you ready, Mr. M-012?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're most welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what is your level of education?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've completed eight years of primary school.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Macedonian State has provided to you, free of charge, elementary education, as to all the other citizens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You were educated in your native language, the Albanian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You have also had the opportunity and the right to vote in the free and direct elections in Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And in the elections, after the establishment of the Autonomous State of Macedonia, in the Parliament there were members of Albanian nationality there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It is also correct that in the government, there are Ministers of Albanian nationality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it so also in the period of 2001, during these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, tell me, do you speak the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I speak Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You have a house where you live together with your wife and your children; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and with my brother. Two brothers live in one house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And in August 2001, you were living in the same house with your brother and his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Today, when you discussed things with my learned colleague, Edina Residovic, you explained to her that the weapons were only a matter of tradition of the Albanian ethnicity in the past. Tell me, do you own some weapons now maybe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never possessed any weapon, and I don't even wish to possess any in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that after the conflict, many people in Ljuboten procured weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have information about this matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Could we now move into a private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, can we agree that the village of Ljuboten is a small community where everyone knows everyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you stated to my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, that you were never a member of a terrorist group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Were your brothers maybe members or supporters of NLA at any time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Were they maybe members or supporters of another terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know any person from Ljuboten who was a member of NLA in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I will now ask you some questions related specifically to the events in the village of Ljuboten in the period between the 10th and the 12th of August. On the Friday, the 10th of August, you were awakened by the shootings around 8.00 in the morning; can we agree with this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: And it is correct that the village was shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You must know where the shells fell inside the village of Ljuboten on the Friday, the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the panoramic photograph of the village of Ljuboten, ERN number N005-7605.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, do you see this photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask for the assistance of the court assistant? I apologise. Could I ask for the assistance of the court assistant? Please help the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, could you mark on this photograph the places where the shells fell on the Friday morning, 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I rise only to assist, perhaps, my colleague. I have been told that it is not possible, for technical reasons, to annotate this panorama. Have I been misinformed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We believe it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. I've been misinformed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness M-012, my question was whether you were able to mark on this photograph the places where the shells fell on the Friday morning, the 10th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please enlarge this photograph? That would enable me to see the houses better, and then I will be in a position to tell you whose house it is. I know where the first shell fell, where this or that person was killed, where the other house was shelled. I know them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we enlarge this photograph a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to see better now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit better. Approximately, now I will tell you the locations, although not 100 per cent accurately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will just ask you to mark the places by writing the numbers from 1 onwards; and when you mark, please tell us what is it -- what is there in that location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I begin?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I mention the names in public of the owners of the houses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a house of Hadji Ismaili. This is where the first shell fell. It should be approximately here near the mosque, although I cannot see it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I think we are not able to see on the photograph the things that you are marking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to see it clearly, either.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you put the number 1 at the first house that you marked and tell us whose house it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the exact house. I cannot define the location where this house is. This photograph is not that clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you approximately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic, could I suggest, it's virtually time now for the second break, that the Chamber has the break, that in that time you might consider how to deal with this? Quite obviously, this picture is one that doesn't enable the witness or any of us to really see a particular house closely. It may be that if half of the photograph is enlarged to the full size of the screen and then separately the other half at a later time, with the witness marking each half, it may be more practical. You might think about that during the break and discuss it with the court staff, and we will resume, then, at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think that we caught a larger part of that photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: A part of the photograph has been enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please circle this photograph and mark with numbers places where the shells fell on the Friday, 10 August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you understood the question I'm asking you about, Friday in the morning, 10 August.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what is there on the place that you are marking, and please mark all the spots with numbers, starting from 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first shell fell on the house of Haxhi Ismaili, and this is the house, at least the way I see it. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the only place on this part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are other places. Shall I pinpoint where they are?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark everything that you see on that part of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It is approximately here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: What was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shells fell there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what was there at the place that you marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A house.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know maybe whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Shall I say the name?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house of Hahxi Meta.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, when you would not be able to see any more places on this part of the photograph, please let us know so we can switch the photographs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may switch it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before doing that, I would ask the Court to tender this photograph as part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D10 [Realtime transcript read in error "2D"], Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I think that the record did not have the entire number of the evidence. It should be 2D10.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. 2D10.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] .

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, do you have in front of you the other part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you circle and mark with numbers here, as well, in the same manner as you did in the previous photograph, and to also tell us what used to be there on those places?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I suggest you commence numbering with number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the mosque is. [Marks] A shell fell here, too. This is the house, the wall (redacted). [Marks] This is where Haxhi Ali was killed, number 4. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will redact the reference to (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we change the photograph now, or do you have more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this part of the photograph in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D11, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we switch the photograph? Could we move the photograph from the mosque towards the right?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You could continue marking here, starting with number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] This is the house. May I mention the name in public?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house of Vejsel. This is number 5. [Marks] This is the house of Nuredin, number 6. [Marks] You may move the picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this part of the photograph in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D12, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The house with number 7 belongs to Haxhi Dalipi. [Marks] I don't recall the other houses. I'm not sure about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this part of the photograph in evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D13, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would that be all or is there another part of the photograph remaining? I think there's one more part outstanding. I apologise. It is all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, you said that the shelling continued until the Sunday morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: That means that the village was shelled also on the Saturday morning or through the entire day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were interruptions in shelling, but, generally, shelling went on from Friday to Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you maybe know the places where the shells fell on Saturday, the 11th of August? Let me clarify. Would you be able to identify in the same way onto the photograph as you indicated about the Friday, 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Would you be able, if I were to show the photograph again from the very beginning, as we did it, to show us where the shells fell on the Saturday, 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Friday, I showed you. For Saturday, I cannot be very accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. M-012, can we agree that the power went off at 10.30 on the Sunday, 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that the power went off at 10.30 on the Sunday, 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was interrupted on Sunday, but I didn't think of looking at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, you have said that you have seen what the members of the Macedonia security forces were wearing on them, what uniforms they wore. Could you tell us, what weapons were they carrying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police forces had automatic rifles in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had, but I didn't have time to look at them properly, as you are asking me to describe to you in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, thank you. Is it true that together with the others, the other members of the village, you were in touch via mobile telephones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have a mobile telephone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that none of the other present persons in the basement of your house had a mobile telephone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you be more precise? Does it mean that they did not have or that they did have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have mobile phones on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move to a private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, the Macedonian security forces, when they entered the yard, you said they ordered you to leave the basement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: To my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, you said today, and also you said today to my learned colleague, Edina Residovic, you said that the members of the security forces forced you to leave the basement through the window and that you wanted to use the door; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the door was blocked with boxes and that for that reason you went out through the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that there were boxes at the door, but they were not that heavy. We could remove them, but they didn't allow us to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, who put those boxes in front of the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, we did. Maybe I was among those who did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Once you left the house, you were told to lie on the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to both men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only to the men.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown the statement given by OSCE [as interpreted]? I think that this is for a private session. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The statement given to the OSCE by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-012, when you started going from your house towards the Ljubanci, were you then accompanied by bulletproof vehicles --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: While walking towards Ljubanci, haven't you seen any other vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our eyes were closed. We didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were taken to the house called "House of Brace," you were again ordered to lie on the ground, face down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, how did the persons who ordered you to do this look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just a few more questions for you. After that, you were taken to the Mirkovci police station, then to the court, and then to the Shutka Prison; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you stated before this Court that you were beaten in the prison as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ZIVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to go into a private session once again briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Ms. Zivkovic. Do I take it there is re-examination, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I would say five to ten minutes' worth, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you can manage it in five minutes, we can probably squeeze it on to the tape, and that is possible because there is no court following us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm going to do the best I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness M-012, you mentioned that on that Sunday in Ljuboten, when the police arrived at your house, one of the elders present in the basement showed a white cloth. Can you tell us, through what part of the house was that cloth shown to the police, that white cloth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white cloth was shown as he took his hand outside the basement window so that they could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Moving on to when you were in -- excuse me. My learned colleague asked you some questions about the photograph of the dead body of Atulla Qaili that I showed to you earlier today, and she mentioned the fact that there was a postmortem cut or incision along the neck. Can you just help us, please? Apart from that incision from the postmortem, in that photograph, would you say Mr. Atulla Qaili looks better, worse, or the same as he did when you last saw him in the garage at Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's who I'm speaking to you. I'm speaking to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photo of Atulla Qaili shows that he's badly -- was mutilated. Every one of us can look at the photo and observe what he went through.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness. Obviously, my question was not clear to you. The photograph that you saw today, did that photograph show how Mr. Qaili looked when you saw him in the basement, or did he look different in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How so? How did he look different in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he seems to have been incised. I don't know by who. I want his photo, the photo of the dead body of Atulla Qaili, to be seen by everyone, everyone to look at the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, we do not have time to hear your comments about what you would like. Apart from the incision on the neck, did the photo look very different from the man you last saw in the basement at the Mirkovci police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were asked about who you -- about the fact that the Minister of Justice in 2001 was an ethnic Albanian. I want to ask you about the time when you were in the court and you were speaking to three people there. What language were they speaking with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what ethnicity these three persons were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My colleague asked you whether you ever wanted to discuss what happened to you in 2001 with the Macedonian police, and you said, "No." My question for you is: While you were in Shutka Prison, did anyone from the police knock on your cell door and ask you to speak with them about these events?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this question has already been answered, because my colleague has asked this in his direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, that's probably right, Ms. Residovic, but carry on, Mr. Saxon, in the interests of speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Has anyone from the police attempted to contact you to ask you about what happened to you in Ljuboten in August 2001 or afterward?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, has anyone contacted -- anyone from the Macedonian police contacted the village leader in Ljuboten to try to arrange to speak with you, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that the home where you and others were sheltering on the 12th of August, 2001 had boxes blocking the door. Just very briefly, why were those boxes put by the door or behind the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were boxes full of clothes, and we put them behind the door to feel safer, because the door was a thin door and we were afraid of shelling. That's why. We wanted to make it more solid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My learned colleague --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My colleague, during her cross-examination, asked you about weapons that were allegedly found in the village of Ljuboten in October 2005, and you were asked to explain who put those weapons there. Can you explain to us, please, now, if you know, how those weapons were there in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Macedonian police intentionally placed them there in order for them to have a case, because one day before the children of the village were playing in that house. If there were weapons there, the children would have found out earlier. It was simply a concoction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This was in October 2005. Can you recall whether this alleged or so-called discovery of weapons in Ljuboten occurred at a time, that month of October, when representatives of this Tribunal were in or visiting the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I am not very sure. But I know that they came afterwards and that they asked us, and we explained what we thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: One last question. The pardon that you received from the Macedonian government while you were in prison, do you remember approximately when you received that pardon and were allowed to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-012 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. On the 10th of December, it was an afternoon. I didn't know I was going to be released by the guards, who threw the door open and said, "Go home. You are the ones we think you are, but it was thanks to the president that you are released."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, thank you very much. You'll be pleased to know that that concludes your questioning. The Chamber would thank you for your assistance and thank you for coming here to The Hague to tell your story. You are now, of course, free to leave and to return to your home, and the Court Officer will show you out in a moment, after the Judges have left. We must now adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m. Thank you again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours, you and The Hague Tribunal, and let justice prevail. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
